passages.text: One afternoon Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
passages.sermon:
Peter and John were two of Jesus’ disciples.
One afternoon, they went to the temple.
They went at the time for prayer.
This was the ninth hour of the day.
passages.original: Πέτρος δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννης ἀνέβαινον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπὶ τὴν ὥραν τῆς προσευχῆς τὴν ἐνάτην

passages.text: And a man who was lame from birth was being carried to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he was put every day to beg from those entering the temple courts.
passages.sermon:
A man could not walk.
He was lame from birth.
People carried him every day.
They brought him to the temple gate.
This gate was called Beautiful.
They placed him there daily.
He begged for money from people entering the temple.
passages.original: καί τις ἀνὴρ χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων ἐβαστάζετο ὃν ἐτίθουν καθ’ ἡμέραν πρὸς τὴν θύραν τοῦ ἱεροῦ τὴν λεγομένην Ὡραίαν τοῦ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην παρὰ τῶν εἰσπορευομένων εἰς τὸ ἱερόν

passages.text: When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he asked them for money.
passages.sermon:
A man was lame from birth.
People carried him to the temple gate every day.
He saw Peter and John.
Peter and John were about to enter the temple.
The man asked Peter and John for money.
passages.original: ὃς ἰδὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην μέλλοντας εἰσιέναι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἠρώτα ἐλεημοσύνην λαβεῖν

passages.text: Peter looked directly at him, as did John. “Look at us!” said Peter.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
John was also an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter looked directly at the lame man.
John looked directly at the lame man.
Peter spoke to the lame man.
Peter said, "Look at us."
passages.original: Ἀτενίσας δὲ Πέτρος εἰς αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ Ἰωάννῃ εἶπεν Βλέψον εἰς ἡμᾶς

passages.text: So the man gave them his attention, expecting to receive something from them.
passages.sermon: The man looked at Peter and John.\r\nHe focused his attention on them.\r\nHe expected to receive something from them.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπεῖχεν αὐτοῖς προσδοκῶν τι παρ’ αὐτῶν λαβεῖν

passages.text: But Peter said, “Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!”
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter spoke to the man who was begging.
Peter said, “I do not have silver.
I do not have gold.
But I will give you what I have.
I give this to you in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth.
Get up.
Walk.”
passages.original: εἶπεν δὲ Πέτρος Ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐχ ὑπάρχει μοι ὃ δὲ ἔχω τοῦτό σοι δίδωμι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει

passages.text: Taking him by the right hand, Peter helped him up, and at once the man’s feet and ankles were made strong.
passages.sermon:
Peter took the man by the right hand.
Peter helped the man stand up.
Immediately, the man’s feet became strong.
Immediately, the man’s ankles became strong.
passages.original: Καὶ πιάσας αὐτὸν τῆς δεξιᾶς χειρὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτόν παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐστερεώθησαν αἱ βάσεις αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ σφυδρά

passages.text: He sprang to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and leaping and praising God.
passages.sermon:
A man could not walk.
\r\nPeter healed him in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth.
\r\nThe man jumped up.
\r\nHe stood.
\r\nHe began to walk.
\r\nHe went with Peter and John into the temple courts.
\r\nHe walked.
\r\nHe leaped.
\r\nHe praised God.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξαλλόμενος ἔστη καὶ περιεπάτει καὶ εἰσῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν περιπατῶν καὶ ἁλλόμενος καὶ αἰνῶν τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: When all the people saw him walking and praising God, they recognized him as the man who used to sit begging at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
passages.sermon:
All the people saw the man.
The man was walking.
The man was praising God.
The people recognized the man.
He was the same man who used to sit and beg at the Beautiful Gate of the temple.
The people were filled with wonder.
The people were amazed at what had happened to him.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶδεν πᾶς ὁ λαὸς αὐτὸν περιπατοῦντα καὶ αἰνοῦντα τὸν Θεόν ἐπεγίνωσκον δὲ αὐτὸν ὅτι οὗτος ἦν ὁ πρὸς τὴν ἐλεημοσύνην καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῇ Ὡραίᾳ Πύλῃ τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν θάμβους καὶ ἐκστάσεως ἐπὶ τῷ συμβεβηκότι αὐτῷ

passages.text: While the man clung to Peter and John, all the people were astonished and ran to them in the walkway called Solomon’s Colonnade.
passages.sermon:
A man had just been healed.
He held tightly to Peter and John.
All the people saw this.
The people were amazed.
They ran to Peter, John, and the man.
They gathered at the walkway called Solomon’s Colonnade.
passages.original: Κρατοῦντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην συνέδραμεν πᾶς ὁ λαὸς πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τῇ στοᾷ τῇ καλουμένῃ Σολομῶντος ἔκθαμβοι

passages.text: And when Peter saw this, he addressed the people: “Men of Israel, why are you surprised by this? Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk?
passages.sermon:
Peter saw the people’s reaction.
Peter spoke to the people.
He spoke to the men of Israel.
Peter asked them a question.
He said, “Men of Israel, why are you surprised by this?”
He asked another question.
He said, “Why do you stare at us?”
He explained the reason for his question.
He said, “You look at us as if we made this man walk.”
He said, “You think we did this by our own power or godliness.”
passages.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος ἀπεκρίνατο πρὸς τὸν λαόν Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται τί θαυμάζετε ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἢ ἡμῖν τί ἀτενίζετε ὡς ἰδίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ εὐσεβείᾳ πεποιηκόσιν τοῦ περιπατεῖν αὐτόν

passages.text: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His servant Jesus. You handed Him over and rejected Him before Pilate, even though he had decided to release Him.
passages.sermon:
The God of Abraham is our God.
The God of Isaac is our God.
The God of Jacob is our God.
He is the God of our fathers.
God glorified His servant Jesus.
You handed Jesus over to others.
You rejected Jesus.
Pilate had decided to release Jesus.
You rejected Jesus in front of Pilate.
passages.original: Ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἐδόξασεν τὸν Παῖδα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν ὃν ὑμεῖς μὲν παρεδώκατε καὶ ἠρνήσασθε κατὰ πρόσωπον Πιλάτου κρίναντος ἐκείνου ἀπολύειν

passages.text: You rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked that a murderer be released to you.
passages.sermon:
You rejected Jesus.
Jesus is the Holy One.
Jesus is the Righteous One.
You asked for a murderer to be released to you.
passages.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ τὸν Ἅγιον καὶ Δίκαιον ἠρνήσασθε καὶ ᾐτήσασθε ἄνδρα φονέα χαρισθῆναι ὑμῖν

passages.text: You killed the Author of life, but God raised Him from the dead, and we are witnesses of the fact.
passages.sermon:
God is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God is the God of our fathers.
God glorified His servant Jesus.
You killed Jesus.
Jesus is the Author of life.
God raised Jesus from the dead.
We are witnesses of this.
passages.original: τὸν δὲ Ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς ἀπεκτείνατε ὃν ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν οὗ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρές ἐσμεν

passages.text: By faith in the name of Jesus, this man whom you see and know has been made strong. It is Jesus’ name and the faith that comes through Him that has given him this complete healing in your presence.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Christ.
You see this man.
You know this man.
This man stands before you.
This man has been made strong.
Faith in the name of Jesus made him strong.
The name of Jesus gave him strength.
Faith that comes through Jesus gave him complete healing.
You all saw this healing happen.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ τοῦτον ὃν θεωρεῖτε καὶ οἴδατε ἐστερέωσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ δι’ αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ τὴν ὁλοκληρίαν ταύτην ἀπέναντι πάντων ὑμῶν

passages.text: And now, brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as did your leaders.
passages.sermon: Brothers, I speak to you now.\r\nI know you acted without understanding.\r\nYour leaders also acted without understanding.
passages.original: Καὶ νῦν ἀδελφοί οἶδα ὅτι κατὰ ἄγνοιαν ἐπράξατε ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὑμῶν

passages.text: But in this way God has fulfilled what He foretold through all the prophets, saying that His Christ would suffer.
passages.sermon:
God spoke through all the prophets.
God foretold that His Christ would suffer.
God has fulfilled these words.
God fulfilled them in this way.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς ἃ προκατήγγειλεν διὰ στόματος πάντων τῶν προφητῶν παθεῖν τὸν Χριστὸν αὐτοῦ ἐπλήρωσεν οὕτως

passages.text: Repent, then, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away, that times of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send Jesus, the Christ, who has been appointed for you.
passages.sermon:
God sent Jesus Christ for you.
God appointed Jesus as the Christ.
Repent now.
Turn back to God.
God will wipe away your sins.
God will bring times of refreshing from His presence.
God will send Jesus Christ to you.
passages.original: μετανοήσατε οὖν καὶ ἐπιστρέψατε πρὸς τὸ ἐξαλειφθῆναι ὑμῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὅπως ἂν ἔλθωσιν καιροὶ ἀναψύξεως ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ἀποστείλῃ τὸν προκεχειρισμένον ὑμῖν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: Heaven must take Him in until the time comes for the restoration of all things, which God announced long ago through His holy prophets.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Christ whom God appointed for you.
Heaven must receive Jesus now.
Heaven will keep Jesus until the time comes to restore all things.
God spoke about this restoration long ago.
God used His holy prophets to announce it.
passages.original: ὃν δεῖ οὐρανὸν μὲν δέξασθαι ἄχρι χρόνων ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων ὧν ἐλάλησεν ὁ Θεὸς διὰ στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ἀπ’ αἰῶνος αὐτοῦ προφητῶν

passages.text: For Moses said, ‘The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to Him in everything He tells you.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of Israel.
Moses spoke to the people of Israel.
Moses said, “The Lord is your God.”
The Lord your God will raise up a prophet for you.
This prophet will come from among your own brothers.
This prophet will be like me, Moses.
You must listen to this prophet.
You must obey everything He tells you.
passages.original: Μωϋσῆς μὲν εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ὑμῶν ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ αὐτοῦ ἀκούσεσθε κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἂν λαλήσῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Everyone who does not listen to Him will be completely cut off from among his people.’
passages.sermon:
God will send a prophet.
This prophet will come from among the people of Israel.
God commands everyone to listen to this prophet.
Anyone who does not listen to this prophet will be cut off from the people.
God will remove that person from among His people.
passages.original: ἔσται δὲ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἥτις ἐὰν μὴ ἀκούσῃ τοῦ προφήτου ἐκείνου ἐξολεθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ

passages.text: Indeed, all the prophets from Samuel on, as many as have spoken, have proclaimed these days.
passages.sermon:
All the prophets spoke about these days.
Samuel was the first of these prophets.
Every prophet after Samuel also spoke about these days.
Each prophet who spoke after Samuel proclaimed these days.
passages.original: Καὶ πάντες δὲ οἱ προφῆται ἀπὸ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν καθεξῆς ὅσοι ἐλάλησαν καὶ κατήγγειλαν τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας

passages.text: And you are sons of the prophets and of the covenant God made with your fathers when He said to Abraham, ‘Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.’
passages.sermon:
You are sons of the prophets.
You are sons of the covenant.
God made this covenant with your fathers.
God spoke to Abraham.
God said to Abraham, “Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.”
passages.original: ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῆς διαθήκης ἧς ὁ Θεὸς διέθετο πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ὑμῶν λέγων πρὸς Ἀβραάμ Καὶ ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου ἐνευλογηθήσονται πᾶσαι αἱ πατριαὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: When God raised up His Servant, He sent Him first to you to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways.”
passages.sermon:
God raised up His Servant Jesus.
God sent Jesus first to you, the people of Israel.
God sent Jesus to bless you.
Jesus blesses you by turning each of you away from your wicked ways.
passages.original: ὑμῖν πρῶτον ἀναστήσας ὁ Θεὸς τὸν Παῖδα αὐτοῦ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν εὐλογοῦντα ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἀποστρέφειν ἕκαστον ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν
